helpDefault.intro: Customize a design in your browser and download a ready-to-print file. Everything runs on your device — your settings never leave it, and it works offline.
licenses.note.scadpub: This configurator itself. ScadPub publishes OpenSCAD models as static, browser-based configurators; its own source is MIT-licensed and available at the link above. The MIT license covers ScadPub's own code only — the bundled components listed below carry their own terms.
licenses.note.openscad: Renders the models in your browser. OpenSCAD is free software under the GNU GPL v2 (or later); the corresponding source is available at the link above. Its build also statically links further third-party libraries (e.g. CGAL, Boost, Eigen, Manifold, FreeType, HarfBuzz, fontconfig, libzip) under their own licenses — see the OpenSCAD source for those.
licenses.note.liberation: Bundled fallback typeface. Any external font a deployment requires (e.g. a license-restricted profile font) is not bundled and is uploaded by you.
licenses.note.atkinson: ScadPub bundles this (via Fontsource) as the interface's own display typeface, for the app chrome.
helpDefault.s1.title: 1. Pick a design
helpDefault.s1.body: Use the design name in the top bar to switch between the available designs.
helpDefault.s2.title: 2. Make it yours
helpDefault.s2.body:
The **Customize** tab lists what you can change, grouped into sections.

- Drag a slider (or type a number), pick from a dropdown, type text, or flip a switch.
- Tap the small **ⓘ** next to a label for a fuller explanation.
- Click a **section header** to fold or unfold it; some start folded.
- Some settings only appear when another one makes them relevant.
- **Find a setting…** narrows the list as you type. A long form also offers **Jump to section** (the list button beside it) to skip straight to one.
- Some designs keep their advanced settings out of the way at first. If you see **Show all settings** — shortened to **+N more** on a phone — that reveals them, and the same control puts them back.
- Once you've changed something, a strip at the **top** of the tab counts your changes and offers **Reset to defaults** (or, with a preset applied, **Revert** to it).
helpDefault.s3.title: 3. Look around the preview
helpDefault.s3.body: **Drag** to spin the model, **scroll or pinch** to zoom, and **right-drag** (or two fingers) to move it.
helpDefault.s4.title: 4. Keep the preview fresh
helpDefault.s4.body:
With **Live preview** on, the model updates a moment after each change. You'll find the switch under the settings panel on a wide screen, and in the **⋮** menu (top right) on a phone.

For slow designs it pauses itself — press **Update** over the preview when you're ready.
helpDefault.s5.title: 5. Save your settings (presets)
helpDefault.s5.body:
The **Presets** tab lists **Ready-made** starting points and the ones **Saved by you** (kept in this browser).

- **Save** keeps your current settings under a name so you can come back to them.
- **Export**/**Import** move saved presets between devices as a file (the same format the desktop OpenSCAD Customizer uses).
helpDefault.s6.title: 6. Import fonts and drawings
helpDefault.s6.body:
Some designs use a file of yours — a font for lettering, or an SVG drawing. You add each one from the control that needs it, not from a separate upload screen:

- **Fonts** (`.ttf`/`.otf`): choose **Import font…** in a design's font menu; the font then shows there by name for every design.
- **Drawings** (`.svg`): use the drawing control's **Prepare SVG…** to bring one in.
- The **Files** action (top bar, or the **⋮** menu on a phone) is where you **manage** what you've imported — see each file's type and size, remove one, or clear all. You don't import from there.
- Files stay in this browser and come back on your next visit; nothing is uploaded.
helpDefault.s7.title: 7. Download & share
helpDefault.s7.body:
The two buttons over the preview:

- **Download for 3D printing** — get the printable file for your slicer.
- **Share** (**Copy link** where your browser can't share directly) — a link that reopens this exact design with your settings.

**Save image**, for a picture of the preview, is in the top bar — or the **⋮** menu on a phone.

If anything needs a look before you download, a coloured pill appears just above those buttons (“1 issue to review”). Tap it — or Download — to open **Review**, which summarises what you're about to get and what's unresolved. Once the model has rendered you can still choose **Download anyway**; while a render has failed, that stays unavailable.
helpDefault.s8.title: 8. Appearance & info
helpDefault.s8.body: The **sun/moon** button switches between light, dark, and automatic, and the **ⓘ** button lists open-source licenses. Both sit in the top bar on a wide screen, and in the **⋮** menu (top right) on a phone.
helpDefault.s9.title: Troubleshooting
helpDefault.s9.body: If the preview fails or looks wrong, open **Messages** (the bell in the top bar) — the design reports what it didn't like there, and the Log tab has the full technical output.
